newsitem.title: GERMANY: Demand for aluminium semis rising in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Demand for aluminium semis rising in Germany.

text.p: Demand for semi-finished aluminium products from German producers picked up in the first quarter of 1997 and is likely to stay firm, the industry association GDA said.

The improvement, which followed a weak 1996, was based on a recovery in economic activity and new applications for aluminium, it said in a statement. The only exception was the ailing building and construction sector, which absorbs 18 percent of aluminium semis.
"Nearly all market segments show increased orders, both at home and abroad," said the head of GDA's semis section, Gerhard Buddenbaum, who is also chairman of Hoogovens Aluminium GmbH.
New domestic orders rose by 12.3 percent in the first quarter, compared with the same 1996 period, while export orders increases by 35.3 percent.

Capacity utilisation was up and lead times were lengthening at the 35 plants represented by GDA. Their combined production in 1996 totalled 1.53 million tonnes of rolled products, extrusions, sections, bars, tubes and forgings -- 4.8 percent less than in 1995.
But first quarter 1997 output was 415,100 tonnes, a 6.4 percent increase over a year earlier.
Buddenbaum said demand for German material from processors in other western European countries had increased and this eased competitive pressure in the lucrative German domestic market.
Semis producers were hoping to increase their sales revenue, which to date was still unsatisfactory.
